docs.summary:
Per-scene navigation state: the registered navmeshes, the query API over them, and (once agents register) the crowd simulation. Owned by [`Navigation`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.UI.Navigation) the same way physics state is owned by [`Physics`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.Resources.Scene~Physics).

Queries are thread-safe: each takes a pooled Detour query under a read lock, so gameplay code may path-find from worker threads. Tile mutations take the write lock and invalidate pooled queries.

members.name: DefaultSettings
members.signature: public static NavMeshWorldSettings DefaultSettings { get; set; }

docs.summary: The settings every new world starts from. Assigning also affects nothing already constructed; use [`ApplySettings`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~ApplySettings) for a live world.
Make `settings` the defaults for new worlds and apply them to the current scene's world.
Copy every tunable from `settings`. Crowd radius and obstacle capacity only reach crowds and navmeshes created afterwards.
How many navmesh polygons one path may cross. See [`MaxPolyPath`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorldSettings~MaxPolyPath).
How many corners one path may have. See [`MaxStraightPath`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorldSettings~MaxStraightPath).
Default half-extents used to snap query positions onto the navmesh, in world units. Larger values tolerate more vertical mismatch but can snap to the wrong floor.

Maximum agent radius the crowds' proximity grids are sized for. Agents with a larger `Radius` degrade neighbour queries silently, so registration warns when one exceeds this. Each crowd reads it at creation.
The crowd steering agents of the given type, or null while none have registered. Advanced use — Prowl agents manage their crowd membership themselves.
The obstacle avoidance tuning agents of the given quality steer with.
Replace the obstacle avoidance tuning for a quality level. Applies to live crowds immediately and to any crowd created later.
Raised when a navmesh registers, before [`NavMeshChanged`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~NavMeshChanged). Main thread.
Raised when a navmesh unregisters, including a rebake replacing it and scene teardown, before [`NavMeshChanged`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~NavMeshChanged). Main thread.
Raised at the start of each navigation update, before the crowd steps.

Raised whenever a navmesh is added, removed, or mutated — including on every frame a carve is still converging, so a listener that only wants the finished result should use [`NavMeshSettled`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~NavMeshSettled).

Raised when queued work finishes and the navmesh is stable again. A carve spans several frames, and anything expensive — re-pathing a crowd, rebuilding a cached triangulation — wants to run once at the end rather than on each of them.

MAY NEVER FIRE: an obstacle moving every frame re-queues work as fast as the pump drains it, so anything that must happen eventually needs its own bound, as the deferred tile swap has.
How many obstacles one navmesh may carve at once, read when a surface registers. A [`NavMeshObstacle`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshObstacle) that enables once the pool is full cuts no hole and warns.
Tiles each instance may rebuild per frame while draining queued carves. Values below 1 are treated as 1.

Instantiate and register a baked navmesh. Returns the instance handle, or null when the data has no tiles, fails to instantiate, or its agent type already has one.

Threading: fires [`NavMeshChanged`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~NavMeshChanged) synchronously on the calling thread, and subscribers (agents, editor overlays) touch the crowd and Transforms — call from the main thread, or guarantee nothing is subscribed. (Queries are the thread-safe surface; registration is not.)
Unregister a navmesh. Blocks until in-flight queries on it finish.
Remove every registered navmesh (scene teardown).
The registered navmesh for an agent type, or null. At most one exists: [`AddNavMeshData`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~AddNavMeshData) refuses a second.

members.name: MutateTileCache
members.signature: public bool MutateTileCache(NavMeshInstance instance, Action<DtTileCache> mutation)

docs.summary:
Run a mutation against an instance's TileCache under the write lock (layer regeneration, bulk obstacle edits). In-flight queries finish first, and pooled queries survive the mutation: a DtNavMeshQuery holds only the mesh reference and node pools it clears on entry.

Threading: fires [`NavMeshChanged`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~NavMeshChanged) synchronously on the calling thread (see [`AddNavMeshData`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~AddNavMeshData) — same main-thread contract).
docs.returns: False when the instance is no longer registered, so the mutation did not run.

docs.summary: The enabled link with the given id in this scene, or null (see [`LinkId`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshLink~LinkId)).
Every enabled link in this scene. What a bake gathers its off-mesh connections from, so it never has to walk the scene to find them.
Every enabled surface in this scene, whether or not it has a navmesh loaded.

docs.summary: Rent a thread-safe query over the agent type's navmesh. Dispose the lease promptly — it holds a read lock that blocks navmesh mutations. Returns false when no navmesh is registered for the agent type.

members.signature: public bool SamplePosition(Float3 sourcePosition, out NavMeshHit hit, float maxDistance, NavMeshQueryFilter filter = default)

docs.summary: Find the closest point on the navmesh within `maxDistance` of `sourcePosition`.

members.name: FindRandomPoint
members.signature: public bool FindRandomPoint(out NavMeshHit hit, NavMeshQueryFilter filter = default)

docs.summary: Pick a random point anywhere on the navmesh. Tiles are picked evenly, then polygons by area within the tile. The point can be on an island the caller cannot walk to, use [`FindRandomPointAround`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~FindRandomPointAround) for one that is reachable.

members.name: FindRandomPointAround
members.signature: public bool FindRandomPointAround(Float3 center, float radius, out NavMeshHit hit, NavMeshQueryFilter filter = default)

docs.summary: Pick a random point within `radius` of `center`, weighted by area. The search walks the navmesh outward from the center, so the point is connected to it and an agent standing at the center can walk there.

members.name: Raycast
members.signature: public bool Raycast(Float3 sourcePosition, Float3 targetPosition, out NavMeshHit hit, NavMeshQueryFilter filter = default)

docs.summary: Trace a walkability ray along the navmesh surface. Returns true when the ray is blocked before the target; `hit` holds the blocking edge either way.
Pass as `maxDistance` (or any non-positive value) to search out to the navmesh's own bounds diagonal, which is by definition the widest gap it can contain.

members.name: FindClosestEdge
members.signature: public bool FindClosestEdge(Float3 sourcePosition, out NavMeshHit hit, float maxDistance, NavMeshQueryFilter filter = default)

docs.summary: Locate the closest navmesh border edge from a point.

params.maxDistance: How far to search. Cost grows with it and an edge beyond it is not found, so pass the widest gap that matters, or [`EdgeSearchDistanceFromBounds`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~EdgeSearchDistanceFromBounds).
params.filter: Which areas and agent type the search uses.

docs.summary: Triangulate the current navmesh for debug drawing or user tooling. Returns an empty triangulation when no navmesh is registered for the agent type — to visualize a baked asset that isn't registered, use [`CalculateTriangulation`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshData~CalculateTriangulation).
Triangulate one registered navmesh. Empty once it has been unregistered.

Advance the navigation world one frame: fires [`PreUpdate`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld~PreUpdate), steps every agent type's crowd, and pumps each TileCache's incremental update (obstacle carving processes a bounded slice of tile rebuilds per frame, amortizing carve cost off the critical path). Called by the scene's variable update.
